notes.omuvuzi: From okuvuga, to drive or ride.
notes.ennimiro: A food garden or small farm.
notes.nkolera: Nkola + -er-: “work for”. More of these in Unit 27.

guidebook.intro: Job titles are people nouns, so they take **omu-** for one person and **aba-** for many. Many come straight from a verb.

tips.title: From verb to job
body: Put **omu-** on a verb stem and change the last **-a** to **-i** to get the person who does it: **-lima** (dig) gives **omulimi** (farmer), **-zimba** (build) gives **omuzimbi** (builder), **-fumba** (cook) gives **omufumbi** (cook).
To say what someone is, drop the first vowel: **Ndi mulimi** (I am a farmer), **Ssali muvuzi** (Ssali is a driver).

culture.title: Everyone farms
body: Even people with office jobs often keep a garden, **ennimiro**, in the village. Weekends “at the farm” are common, and the harvest feeds the family in town.

culture.title: Gyebale ko again
body: Remember **Gyebale ko** from Unit 1? It thanks someone for their work. Say it to any worker you meet: the builder, the trader, the cook.
